standard.title: Experiment to refine skills and develop personal expression
standard.description: experiment with visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to refine skills and develop personal expression
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can experiment with and document visual arts processes and reflect on discoveries to make informed choices (AC9AVA8D01, implied from progression). They have developed documentation habits. They have not yet investigated a medium in depth for comprehensive understanding, or begun identifying an emerging personal style.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with visual conventions, processes and materials to refine skills and develop personal expression, using deep investigation and documentation to identify their own artistic voice.

nodes.label: In-depth investigation of a medium
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate a medium or form in depth — exploring its material properties and technical processes comprehensively, developing understanding of what it can do.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one medium's material properties and at least two technical processes associated with it; document discoveries.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment comprehensively with a medium's material properties and technical processes; investigate how these properties enable specific visual effects; document and evaluate the investigation; develop understanding of the full range of what the medium can do.
wider: Investigate artists through their sketchbooks — uncover their experimental processes and find connections between their practice and the development of their personal expression

Use line analysis (drawing lines, shapes and arrows over photocopies of artworks) to decode compositional techniques — use a coding system for rule of thirds, movement, repetition and visual hierarchy; apply findings to your own work
nodes.hinge_reason: Comprehensive medium understanding is the foundation for technical refinement — students who have only surface-level material knowledge cannot make the nuanced choices that distinguish personal expression from generic making. Depth here enables everything downstream.

response_modes.reason: In-depth investigation of a single medium requires extended practice — not one lesson but sustained engagement. The consolidation is not about drilling a single technique but about building comprehensive knowledge through varied experimentation within one form.

success_criteria: Investigates at least two technical processes of one medium
Documents what the medium can and cannot do based on the investigation

nodes.label: Interrogating multiple approaches
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interrogate multiple approaches to representing a topic — using different media to express different interpretations or emotions.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two different media to represent the same topic differently; describe what each approach expresses.
nodes.typical_width: Interrogate multiple approaches to the same activity using diverse media; produce several works on the one topic each exploring a different emotion or interpretation; compare approaches and document what each reveals.
wider: Develop an 'inspiration' journal — collect photographs, found objects, media experiments, thoughts and ideas from everyday life; use Viewpoints questions to identify what you are drawn to and why

Investigate artists from a different cultural context (e.g. a country in the Asia region) through accounts of their influences — reflect on how their accounts inform your understanding of what can shape your own practice

response_modes.reason: Using a single approach to represent a topic produces one reading. The comparison across multiple media reveals how mode shapes meaning — students who only use one approach cannot see the expressive choices available to them.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The inspiration journal practice and the multi-cultural artist investigation are particularly rich directions — both help students identify their own aesthetic preferences, which is the foundation of personal expression rather than technical competence alone.
success_criteria: Uses at least two different media to represent the same topic
Describes what each approach expresses differently — not just what it looks like but what it communicates

nodes.label: Developing personal expression
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and document an emerging personal style — patterns in what they are drawn to, how they work, and what visual choices feel distinctively their own.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one pattern in their visual arts practice that could characterise an emerging personal style.
nodes.typical_width: Use Viewpoints questions to interrogate an inspiration journal and documented practice to identify emerging preferences and style characteristics; document personal style development; ask 'What am I drawn to and why is this important to me?'
wider: Annotate photocopies of artworks you admire with compositional analysis — identify patterns in what you respond to and connect these to patterns in your own making
Investigate the development of a visual arts form you work in — trace how personal expression has developed within this form historically and reflect on where your own practice sits

response_modes.reason: Medium investigation, multi-approach interrogation and emerging preferences come together in the identification of personal expression. The integration is the recognition: 'Here is what my practice is becoming and why.'

success_criteria: Identifies at least one pattern in their practice that could characterise an emerging personal style
Can explain what they are drawn to and connect it to choices visible in their work
